issues.legal_issue: A tenant directly affected by a property-tax assessment may complain about the assessment and appeal it, subject to the applicable procedural requirements.
material_facts: The tenants were exposed to the property-tax burden because rent could be increased to reflect increased taxes, because an agreement placed the tax obligation on tenants, or because the corporation could seek payment from an occupier if the primarily liable person did not pay.
The statutory appeal provisions did not confine appeals to owners, and the assessment rules permitted complaints by owners or occupiers.

The appeal required compliance with procedural conditions, including deposit of the disputed tax; a tenant who had not filed the complaint leading to the decision needed leave of the appellate court to appeal.
issues.conclusion: Tenants directly affected by the assessment may complain and appeal, provided they comply with the applicable procedural conditions; a tenant who did not file the complaint must obtain leave to appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 139, 140, 406 and 407 of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949, read with the taxation rules and Section 10 of the Bombay Rent Act, a person aggrieved by an assessment may appeal even where the appeal provision does not expressly identify who may appeal. The tenant’s direct exposure to the tax burden supports standing, but does not dispense with the statutory conditions for appeal. The Court analogized the appeal right to the right under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure: an affected person may appeal subject to the conditions attached to that right.

predicates.property_tax_assessment_challenge: A proceeding challenges the assessment or enhancement of property tax on premises occupied by a tenant.
predicates.tenant_directly_bears_or_is_exposed_to_t: The tenant bears, or is directly exposed to, the tax burden through a legal liability, a rent increase, or an agreement with the landlord.
predicates.tenant_complied_with_appeal_requirements: The tenant followed the applicable complaint and appeal procedures, including obtaining leave to appeal if the tenant did not file the complaint that preceded the appeal.

issues.definition: When a tenant directly bears or is exposed to the tax burden in a property-tax assessment challenge and complies with the applicable appeal requirements, the tenant may maintain the challenge.

issues.legal_issue: Where standard rent has not been fixed for let premises, actual rent received is the annual rent used to determine annual letting value, subject to the authority to disregard a rent figure that is not genuine.
material_facts: The premises were let and no standard rent had been fixed under the rent-control legislation.
The municipal enactment deemed the rent actually received to be the reasonably expected annual rent notwithstanding other law.

A related proviso allowed the Commissioner to disregard the stated rent if it was less than the reasonably expected rent; the Court understood that power to address a false or non-genuine rent figure.
issues.conclusion: For premises covered by the proviso, actual rent received is the basis for determining annual letting value when standard rent has not been fixed, unless the stated rent is not genuine and the related proviso applies.
issues.legal_principle: Proviso (aa) to Section 2(1A)(ii) of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 expressly makes actual rent received the deemed annual rent notwithstanding other law, where standard rent has not been fixed under Section 11 of the Bombay Rent Act. The Court applied Municipal Corporation, Indore v. Ratna Prabha, which gave effect to a comparable non-obstante clause, and distinguished Corporation of Calcutta v. Padma Debi, Corporation of Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation of India, Guntur Municipal Council v. Guntur Town Rate Payers’ Association, Dewan Daulat Rai Kapoor v. New Delhi Municipal Committee and Morvi Municipality v. State of Gujarat, because the provisions considered in those cases lacked the relevant non-obstante clause. The related proviso (aaa) permits rejection of a rent figure that is not genuine.

rule.if: municipal_property_tax_valuation and premises_are_let and standard_rent_has_not_been_fixed and actual_rent_is_genuinely_received

predicates.municipal_property_tax_valuation: A proceeding determines the annual letting value for municipal property-tax purposes.
predicates.premises_are_let: The premises are occupied under a letting arrangement.
predicates.standard_rent_has_not_been_fixed: No standard rent has been fixed for the premises under the applicable rent-control process.
predicates.actual_rent_is_genuinely_received: The rent put forward is the genuine rent actually received, rather than a false figure intended to evade the correct assessment.

issues.definition: For a municipal property-tax valuation of let premises, if standard rent has not been fixed and the stated actual rent is genuine, that rent is the basis for annual letting value.

issues.legal_issue: A special notice concerning a proposed change to an assessment need not set out the grounds or calculation details if it identifies the nature of the assessment entry.
material_facts: A tenant challenged a special written notice concerning an assessment change because it did not state the particulars or grounds on which the assessment was to be enhanced.
The notice requirement called for the nature of the entry to be specified, and the assessment rules allowed the person concerned to complain and seek clarification at the ensuing hearing.
issues.conclusion: The notice was not invalid merely because it omitted the grounds or calculation details, provided it specified the nature of the entry.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rule 15(2) of Chapter VIII of Schedule A to the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949, read with Rules 9, 13 and 18, a special notice must specify the nature of the assessment entry. It need not provide additional particulars explaining how the rateable value was calculated; the person notified may complain and present evidence, and clarification may be sought at the hearing.

predicates.special_notice_challenges_an_assessment_: A special notice informs an owner or occupier about a proposed change to an assessment.
predicates.notice_identifies_the_nature_of_the_entr: The notice states the nature of the entry made in the assessment record.
predicates.notice_omits_detailed_grounds_or_calcula: The notice does not explain the detailed grounds or calculations used to arrive at the assessment.

issues.definition: A special notice is not invalid for omitting detailed grounds or calculations if it identifies the nature of the assessment entry.
